chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from Abd al-Rahman ibn Hammad from Ziyad al-Qandi from al-Husayn al-Sahhaf from Sadir said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): What is incumbent upon a man in seeking sustenance? He said: 'When you open your door and spread your mat, you have fulfilled what is upon you.'

key_terms.قَضَيْتَ مَا عَلَيْكَ: You have fulfilled what is upon you

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum requirement for a Muslim to fulfill in order to legitimately seek sustenance according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the religious obligation regarding sustenance is fulfilled by the act of making oneself available and ready for work, symbolized by opening one's door and spreading one's mat. This emphasizes that divine provision is contingent upon human effort and initiative, a core principle in Shia jurisprudence distinguishing between the duty to seek (*talab*) and the guarantee of receipt. It serves as a practical guideline for believers to balance trust in God (*tawakkul*) with active participation in the economic sphere.
